newsitem.title: USA: Miami Int'l Airport night flight ban proposed.
newsitem.headline: Miami Int'l Airport night flight ban proposed.

text.p: Dade County, Florida, Commissioner Bruce Kaplan has proposed a resolution to ban night flights at Miami International Airport.
Cargo carriers which often operate at night, oppose the proposal which Kaplan's spokeswoman Alice Aidalgo-Gato said will come before the county commission's aviation committee sometime this week.
"The first step is that a study needs to be done. This begins the process," Aidalgo-Gato said.
"We would not like this," said Guillermo Mejia, the Miami- based commercial director for Colombian all-cargo Tampa Airlines.

"Most of the cargo that comes into Miami is perishable and it has to arrive in the cooler weather at night," Mejia said. If the flowers, fruits, vegetables and fish were to land in the heat of the day it would affect the product, Mejia said.
"You would also have more congestion during the day, affecting safety and everything else," he said.
MIA has 71 arrivals and 23 departures between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m., the hours of the proposed ban, a Dade County Aviation spokesman said Monday.
Of the 71 arrivals, 38 are cargo and general aviation flights, the spokesman said. Of the 23 departures, 18 are cargo and small aircraft.
